43424-francisco-our-little-argentine-cou.title: Francisco Our Little Argentine Cousin
43424-francisco-our-little-argentine-cou.creator: Eva Cannon Brooks
43424-francisco-our-little-argentine-cou.description: A book by Eva Cannon Brooks. IF you take a steamer in New York whose destination is the eastern coast of South America, and remain on it a little over four weeks, you will reach the great metropolis of our twin continent, Buenos Aires.

arxiv-2011-06143.title: Adaptive Central-Upwind Scheme on Triangular Grids for the Saint-Venant System
arxiv-2011-06143.creator: Yekaterina Epshteyn 1 and Thuong Nguyen
arxiv-2011-06143.description: Abstract In this work we develop a robust adaptive well-balanced and positivity-preserving central-upwind scheme on unstructured triangular grids for shallow water equations. The numerical method is an extension of the scheme from [ Liu et al. ,J. of Comp. Phys, 374 (2018), pp. 213 - 236].

arxiv-2105-11493.title: Towards Precision Aquaculture: A High Performance, Cost-effective IoT approach
arxiv-2105-11493.creator: Rafael R. Teixeira, Juliana B. Puccinelli Luis Poersch, Marcelo R. Pias and Vinícius M. Oliveira, Ahmed Janati, Maxime Paris
arxiv-2105-11493.description: Abstract Demand for ocean-based high-quality and sustainable fish protein soared in the last decade. Unlike precision agriculture, aquaculture remains an under-equipped farming activity. To fully realise a vision of precision aquaculture , smart IoT can offer the essential tools to local producers worldwide.

arxiv-2205-06564.title: An Ethical Black Box for Social Robots: a draft Open Standard
arxiv-2205-06564.creator: Alan F.T. Winfield, Anouk van Maris, Pericle Salvini, Marina Jirotka
arxiv-2205-06564.description: Abstract This paper introduces a draft open standard for the robot equivalent of an aircraft flight data recorder, which we call an ethical black box. This is a device, or software module, capable of securely recording operational data (sensor, actuator and control decisions) for a social robot, in order to support the investigation of accidents or near-miss incidents.

arxiv-2208-06918.title: Gradient Mask: Lateral Inhibition Mechanism Improves Performance in Artificial Neural Networks
arxiv-2208-06918.creator: Lei Jiang, Yongqing Liu, Shihai Xiao, Yansong Chua
arxiv-2208-06918.description: Abstract Lateral inhibitory connections have been observed in the cortex of the biological brain, and has been extensively studied in terms of its role in cognitive functions. However, in the vanilla version of backpropagation in deep learning, all gradients (which can be understood to comprise of both signal and noise gradients) flow through the network during weight updates.

arxiv-2301-04259.title: SOAP-GPU: Efficient Spectral Modelling of Stellar Activity Using Graphical Processing Units
arxiv-2301-04259.creator: Yinan Zhao, Xavier Dumusque
arxiv-2301-04259.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yinan Zhao, Xavier Dumusque. Stellar activity mitigation is one of the major challenges for the detection of earth-like exoplanets in radial velocity measurements. Several promising techniques are now investigating the use of spectral time-series, to differentiate between stellar and planetary perturbations. In this context, developing a software that can efficiently explore the parameter space of stellar activity at the spectral level is of great importance.

arxiv-2301-12465.title: Kinetic reconstruction of free energies as a function of multiple order parameters
arxiv-2301-12465.creator: Yagyik Goswami, Srikanth Sastry
arxiv-2301-12465.description: Abstract A vast array of phenomena, ranging from chemical reactions to phase transformations, are analysed in terms of a free energy surface defined with respect to a single or multiple order parameters. Enhanced sampling methods are typically used, especially in the presence of large free energy barriers, to estimate free energies using biasing protocols and sampling of transition paths.

arxiv-2309-04619.title: High-entropy effect at rare-earth site in DyNi
arxiv-2309-04619.creator: Yuito Nakamura, Koshin Takeshita, Terukazu Nishizaki, Jiro Kitagawa
arxiv-2309-04619.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuito Nakamura, Koshin Takeshita, Terukazu Nishizaki, Jiro Kitagawa. We report the structural and magnetic properties of RNi (R=Dy, Tb 1/3 Dy 1/3 Ho 1/3 , and Gd 1/5 Tb 1/5 Dy 1/5 Ho 1/5 Er 1/5 ) to investigate the high-entropy effect at the rare-earth site. The lattice parameters are almost unchanged by the increase of configurational entropy, which is due to the successive partial substitution of Dy by pair of rare earth elements located on both sides of Dy in the periodic table.

arxiv-2404-17770.title: Interfaces as transport barriers in two-dimensional Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes turbulence
arxiv-2404-17770.creator: Nadia Bihari Padhan, Rahul Pandit
arxiv-2404-17770.description: Abstract We investigate the role of interfaces as transport barriers in binary-fluid turbulence by employing Lagrangian tracer particles. The Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes (CHNS) system of partial differential equations provides a natural theoretical framework for our investigations. For specificity, we utilize the two-dimensional (2D) CHNS system.

arxiv-2502-13694.title: Natural damping of time-harmonic waves and its influence on Schwarz methods
arxiv-2502-13694.creator: Martin Gander \orcidID 0000-0001-8450-9223 and Hui Zhang \orcidID 0000-0001-7245-0674
arxiv-2502-13694.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The Helmholtz equation (\Delta+\omega^{2})u=f is often used as the prototype time harmonic problem which is difficult to solve by numerical methods, both because high mesh resolutions are required when the wave number \omega becomes large and iterative solvers struggle to solve such discretized problems ernst2011difficult .

arxiv-2511-04539.title: Unified Generative Latent Representation for Functional Brain Graphs
arxiv-2511-04539.creator: Subati Abulikemu, Tiago Azevedo, Michail Mamalakis, John Suckling
arxiv-2511-04539.description: Abstract Functional brain graphs are often characterized with separate graph-theoretic or spectral descriptors, overlooking how these properties covary and partially overlap across brains and conditions. We anticipate that dense, weighted functional connectivity graphs occupy a low-dimensional latent geometry along which both topological and spectral structures display graded variations.

arxiv-2512-05221.title: Benchmarking Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Supported Nanoparticles: Decoupling Energy Accuracy from Structural Exploration
arxiv-2512-05221.creator: Jiayan Xu, Abhirup Patra, Amar Deep Pathak, Sharan Shetty, Detlef Hohl, Roberto Car
arxiv-2512-05221.description: Abstract Supported nanoparticle catalysts are widely used in the chemical industry. Computational modeling of supported nanoparticles based on density functional theory (DFT) often involves structural searches of stable local minimum energy configurations and molecular dynamics simulations at finite temperature. These are computationally demanding tasks that are intractable within DFT for large systems.

pmc-10644879.creator: Bruce Twinamasiko, Andrew Mutekanga, Olilanya Ogueri, Nakitto Irene Kisakye, Crystal M North, Conrad Muzoora, Daniel Muyanja
pmc-10644879.description: PurposeChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. In this paper, we determined risk factors for COPD among patients presenting to pulmonology and medical outpatients’ clinics of Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital (MRRH).MethodsIn this case–control study, cases were patients with COPD confirmed by spirometry and controls were those with normal spirometry.

pmc-10876025.title: Risk factors for carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infections in Intensive Care Units: a multicentre case-control study with a competing-risks analysis
pmc-10876025.creator: FERHAT ARSLAN, ECE AKBULUT, SENİHA SENBAYRAK, ASU ÖZGÜLTEKİN, SEBAHAT AKSARAY, HAYRİYE CANKAR DAL, HASAN OKTAY EMİR, HANDAN ANKARALI, ALI MERT, HALUK VAHABOGLU
pmc-10876025.description: SummaryAimThis study investigated the risk factors for the development of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) infections in adult patients in Intensive Care Units (ICUs).MethodsA multicentre case-control study was conducted in ICUs in three tertiary hospitals in Turkey. The cases were patients culture-confirmed CRKP and a condition associated with healthcare-associated infections.

pmc-12429360.title: Trends in Sports-Related Upper Extremity Injuries Presenting to United States Emergency Departments: A Retrospective Analysis of National Injury Data
pmc-12429360.creator: Matthew D. Ramey, Srivatsan J. Swaminathan, Auston R. Locke, Niklas H. Koehne, Christoph A. Schroen, Visweshwar G. Swaminathan, John J. Corvi, Salvatore Capotosto, Paul J. Cagle, Michael R. Hausman
pmc-12429360.description: Background: Across many sports, injuries to the upper extremity (UE) are prevalent due to falls on an outstretched hand (FOOSH) and overuse. This retrospective analysis aimed to characterize sports-related UE injuries in the United States (US) over the past decade, examining injury frequency, affected body part, diagnosis, and hospital disposition across age, sex, and sport.

pmc-12516017.title: Coordinated Transcriptomic and Epigenetic Approach Reveals Molecular Features Underlying Natural Mating Ability in Captive Male Giant Pandas
pmc-12516017.creator: Zheng Yan, Yinghu Lei, Pengpeng Zhao, Danhui Zhang, Jiena Shen, Guiquan Zhang, Rongping Wei, Mingyue Zhang, Dingzhen Liu
pmc-12516017.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Natural mating ability is a critical behavioral trait for the reproductive success of captive endangered mammals, and its loss often reflects declining adaptability and potential physiological dysfunctions. However, the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we integrated blood transcriptome and whole‐genome DNA methylation (whole‐genome bisulfite sequencing) data to systematically explore the molecular basis of natural mating ability differences in captive male giant pandas ( Ailuropoda melanoleuca ).

pmc-12669021.title: Targeting FZD6 creates therapeutically actionable vulnerabilities for advanced prostate cancer
pmc-12669021.creator: Yongtao Li, Zhicheng Zhou, Yiqun Zhang, Deyong Jia, Ding Wang, Mary C Reiger, Chad J Creighton, Peter S Nelson, Eva Corey, Colm Morrissey, Li Xin
pmc-12669021.description: Wnt signaling is a complex pathway consisting of numerous ligands and frizzled (FZD) receptors. These signaling components are widely expressed in human prostate tissues and often undergo upregulation or mutation in advanced prostate cancers. Enhanced Wnt signaling promotes prostate cancer cell proliferation, metastasis, and resistance to therapy. However, targeting pan-Wnt signaling poses challenges due to tissue toxicity.

pmc-12960063.title: Different types of exercise and myocardial angiogenesis regulation: A scoping review of cardiac‐specific evidence in animal models
pmc-12960063.creator: Putri Karisa, Nova Sylviana, Aziiz Mardanarian Rosdianto, Hanna Goenawan, Mas Rizky Anggun Adipurna Syamsunarno, Setiawan
pmc-12960063.description: Exercise promotes myocardial angiogenesis, yet molecular responses vary by modality, and cardiac‐specific evidence in healthy models remains fragmented. This study aimed to map biomolecular regulators of myocardial/coronary angiogenesis across exercise types in healthy animal models. PRISMA‐ScR scoping review. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and SpringerLink.

pmc-12983305.title: Orthogonal Biosynthesis of Pyrrolamides through Dehydration by a Pathway-Specific Glycoside Hydrolase-Like Enzyme in Gram-Positive Bacteria
pmc-12983305.creator: Daichi Kanki, Sumire Kurosawa, Ayako Yoshida, Takayoshi Awakawa, Saori Kosono, Makoto Nishiyama
pmc-12983305.description: Pyrrolamides, defined by a pyrrole-2-carboxamide core, represent a family of natural products produced by Streptomyces species. They exhibit potent yet promiscuous bioactivities, including antimicrobial, antifungal, antiviral, and anticancer effects. The characteristic pyrrole moiety is derived from 4-acetamidopyrrole-2-carboxylate, which was previously proposed to originate most likely from N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate.

pmc-13256035.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals the Role of the Gut Microbiota–Metabolite–Endocrine Axis in Post-Weaning Estrus Recovery in Tibetan Pigs
pmc-13256035.creator: Jian Zhang, Dong Yang, Mengjia Han, Mengqi Duan, Hongliang Zhang, Peng Shang
pmc-13256035.description: Simple SummaryReproductive performance is a key factor affecting the efficiency of Tibetan pig production, and the weaning-to-estrus interval (WEI) is widely used to evaluate sow fertility. However, some Tibetan sows fail to return to estrus after weaning, which limits their reproductive performance, and the underlying causes remain unclear.

pmc-13372027.creator: Hussam Ali, Ernesto Cristiano, Pierpaolo Lupo, Sara Foresti, Guido De Ambroggi, Silvia Magnani, Maria Giovanna Bucci, Eduardo Celentano, Riccardo Cappato

Despite the rapid expansion of PFA and numerous studies and registries, only a limited number of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) provide a head-to-head comparison between PFA and thermal AF ablation. The aim of this Rapid Communication is to collect evidence-based data from available RCTs evaluating PFA vs.

pmc-13521238.title: Targeted blood-brain barrier penetration for traumatic brain injury therapy via RXR/PPAR-driven microglial M2 polarization
pmc-13521238.creator: Songyu Chen, Junyu Lin, Xiaxuan Zhang, Lin Zhou, Zhicheng Xu, Xiao Hou, Dongming Gao, Liang Gao, Lei Li
pmc-13521238.description: As a leading global cause of death and disability, traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a complex secondary injury process leading to long-term neurological impairment. Current therapeutic efficacy is limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the absence of integrated approaches to address neuroinflammation and neuroregeneration.

pmc-13588338.title: Knowledge and attitude among the mothers of children in age group 1–5 years regarding childhood hearing loss
pmc-13588338.creator: Anushree Bhagavan, Adithya Sreedharan Sanitha, Dhanshree Rajesh Gunjawate, Rohit Ravi
pmc-13588338.description: AimsThe present study aims to explore the knowledge and attitudes among the mothers of children aged 1–5 years regarding childhood hearing loss, its risk factors, effects, and acceptance.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among mothers of children aged 1–5 years using convenience sampling.

pmc-13602966.title: College students’ psychological resilience and daily recovery: a narrative review
pmc-13602966.creator: Chao Li
pmc-13602966.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Research on college students’ psychological resilience has long focused on stable protective and risk factors at the individual level, while paying insufficient attention to the recovery processes in response to daily micro-stressful contexts. Framed by the Conservation of Resources theory, this narrative review reconceptualizes resilience as the long-term outcome of sustained successful adaptation to everyday demands, a capacity that a daily recovery process helps to build and maintain.
